prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory when capability<dispatch target; applies accepted ceiling). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; blocks protection conflicts; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace). Substation Operator: switching, clearances; modes Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint. Grid Dispatcher: targets. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard; updated on confirmed vessel/task changes). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; repair prioritization), Work Permit Portal (Isolation Boundary Sketch; status reviewed before departure), Personnel Tracking Console (reconciled with approved crew list before boarding), Warehouse System (cargo prep before berth). Weather Service, Metocean Buoy, Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note). Modes: Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum, Crew Count Correction; confirms arrival/departure vs limits. Service Operations Vessel: Recovery Basket Load Sheet; Crew Transfer Vessel. Marine Coordinator: accountability, berth view, uses Berth Slot Confirmation; resolves berth conflicts by urgency, compatibility, delay impact; may resequence lower priority preserving rest/inspections; disruption: later slot, other berth, standby. Field Supervisor: accountability, cyber briefings, close-access findings documented. Cyber: Cybersecurity Gateway monitors; Cybersecurity Analyst: Firmware Hash Attestation; isolate only affected connection; SCADA Engineer validates restoration. Duty Planner: prioritizes, repair windows, crews/vessels, checks task vs work authorization and resources. Maintenance starts only after scope, route, supervisor confirmed. Blade Specialist: classifies, NDT, defect records, verifies repairs. Close access only after

New part:
S493: The Field Supervisor reviews the worksite limits with the crew before anyone enters the controlled area.
S494: Physical boundaries are marked so that the work area and any adjacent operating equipment are clearly distinguishable.
S495: The crew confirms that the marked limits match the current isolation points and the approved maintenance scope.
S496: The Electrical Technician verifies electrical isolation at the work location before work on electrical equipment begins.
S497: The Substation Operator confirms that switching conditions affecting the worksite are understood by the relevant personnel.
S498: The Vessel Master confirms that the vessel is safely positioned and that transfer conditions remain acceptable.
S499: The Marine Coordinator suspends access when sea or weather conditions make transfer unsafe.
S500: A Weather Hold remains in effect until the responsible operational authority confirms that conditions permit work to proceed.
S501: Personnel use the North Access Scanner or South Access Scanner at the designated entry point.
S502: The Personnel Tracking Console is checked to confirm that people entering and leaving the site are accounted for.
S503: The Field Supervisor verifies each worker's authorization, competence, and fitness for the assigned task.
S504: Before starting, the crew inspects personal protective equipment, communications equipment, and rescue equipment for serviceability.
S505: The HSE Officer checks that emergency routes, muster points, and rescue arrangements are understood by everyone at the worksite.
S506: The crew tests the required radio channel with the Operations Radio Console before separating into work teams.
S507: Tools and loose materials are secured against dropped-object hazards and movement caused by vessel motion.
S508: Access to the worksite is restricted to personnel listed for the task, and visitors remain under escort.
S509: The Field Supervisor pauses the job if actual conditions differ from the approved method or the marked worksite boundaries.
S510: Any change to the work scope requires a renewed safety review before affected work resumes.
S511: The crew maintains clear access to fire equipment, escape routes, and lifting areas throughout the task.
S512: At shift handover, the outgoing supervisor briefs the incoming supervisor on site conditions, access status, and outstanding hazards.
S513: Work is closed out only after personnel are accounted for, equipment is removed or secured, and the worksite is left in a safe condition.
S514: Switching coordination begins with a defined operational need, a safe sequence, and an agreed period for execution.
S515: The Duty Planner develops the proposed sequence with the Control Engineer and identifies affected equipment and operating limits.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
